catalog:medication:paracetamol.evidenceSummary: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) has an FDA-approved label; the linked one covers the intravenous form for mild to moderate pain, for moderate to severe pain alongside opioids, and for fever. The label carries a boxed warning about dosing errors and about acute liver failure, mostly when more than the recommended maximum is taken or when several paracetamol-containing products are combined. A 2026 review of cancer pain says the evidence for paracetamol there is limited and of low quality, with little added benefit next to strong opioids. Nothing in these links supports a specific rate of liver injury at normal use.

catalog:medication:antacid.evidenceSummary: Proton pump inhibitors block the H+/K+-ATPase pump in stomach parietal cells and so reduce acid. A 2025 review describes them as widely prescribed for reflux, peptic ulcer disease and prevention of gastrointestinal bleeding. The same review lists interactions, including omeprazole reducing the effect of clopidogrel, and links long-term use to vitamin B12 and calcium deficiency, fractures and more infections. This is a general review, not a regulator label or a trial.

Omeprazole reduces the effect of clopidogrel.

verdict.bottomLine: Proton pump inhibitors cut stomach acid; long-term use is linked to nutrient deficiency, fractures and infections.

catalog:supplement:glycine.evidenceSummary: Glycine is an amino acid studied for sleep. Small human trials from one research group report better subjective sleep quality in people who sleep poorly, and less fatigue with better psychomotor vigilance after nights of restricted sleep. Rat experiments point to a fall in core body temperature through NMDA receptors in the suprachiasmatic nucleus as the mechanism. The human evidence is limited to a few small studies; nothing here covers athletic use.

catalog:supplement:casein-protein.evidenceSummary: Casein is a slow-digesting milk protein. Randomised crossover trials in small groups of healthy men show that how casein is processed changes how quickly amino acids appear in the blood, with cross-linked sodium caseinate fastest. In older men, casein taken in a milk matrix slowed digestion but did not change muscle protein synthesis afterwards. A trial comparing cow and goat casein found similar stomach emptying, with higher essential amino acids after cow casein. These are small mechanistic trials, not strength or body-composition studies.

A 24-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 164 adults found that magnesium citrate, oxide and sulfate did not change arterial stiffness or blood pressure, although citrate raised blood and urine magnesium most. A rat study found that different organic forms reach different tissues, with behaviour changes in animals. No human trial here shows an anxiety or blood-pressure benefit.

catalog:supplement:vitamin-e.evidenceSummary: Vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant; alpha-tocopherol is the only form counted as essential. A Nordic Nutrition Recommendations scoping review reports that dietary vitamin E may help prevent some chronic disease, but that there is no clear benefit from alpha-tocopherol supplements in generally healthy people, and that deficiency is rare and usually has other causes. An EFSA scientific opinion keeps the existing tolerable upper intake levels, with impaired blood clotting and bleeding as the critical effect of excess. Both are reviews and guidance, not trials.

A second systematic review of nine trials found cortisol fell without significant harm, but no study looked at what lowering cortisol does to adrenal function or at long-term use. Trials are short and use different preparations.

catalog:exercise:cardio-zone2.evidenceSummary: Zone 2 means steady aerobic exercise just below the first lactate or ventilatory threshold, as an expert panel of coaches and scientists defines it. A 2025 narrative review concludes that current evidence does not make Zone 2 the best intensity for mitochondrial or cardiorespiratory gains, and that higher intensities do at least as well, especially when training time is short. A laboratory study of 50 cyclists found the markers used to set Zone 2 vary widely between individuals. The expert panel also notes the expected adaptations are probably not unique to this intensity.

protocols.regimen: continuous, variable or interval-type sessions at intensities immediately below the first lactate or ventilatory threshold
protocols.outcome: The panel expected a broad range of central and peripheral adaptations, and noted these may not be unique to this intensity.

catalog:exercise:swimming.evidenceSummary: Swimming is whole-body aerobic exercise done in water. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 trials found aquatic exercise reduced mood and anxiety symptoms (standardised mean difference -0.77), though the swimming-only subgroup was not statistically significant. A quasi-experimental study in 40 adults with type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure reported improvements in cholesterol and other metabolic risk factors after regular swimming. A systematic review of 20 non-randomised studies in early adolescents reports better cardiorespiratory fitness and bone and body-composition outcomes, but rated most studies at high risk of bias.

catalog:exercise:hiking.evidenceSummary: Hiking is long, low-intensity walking outdoors. An integrative review reports better cardiovascular function, lower chronic disease risk, better immune function, lower stress and improved mood among hikers, and social benefits too. A cross-sectional study using exercise testing on real trails found that effort and cardiorespiratory strain vary widely between people and routes, so generic trail advice fits poorly. The evidence is reviews and observational work, not controlled trials, and a popular-science article covers the same ground.

Its systolic blood pressure estimate was not statistically significant overall, with a reduction appearing only in whole-body heating subgroups. A meta-analysis of infrared sauna in heart failure found lower B-type natriuretic peptide and better left-ventricular ejection fraction, with evidence strength rated moderate to insufficient. A cohort of 2277 men found frequent sauna bathing together with higher fitness was associated with lower cardiovascular and all-cause mortality.

A systematic review of 58 studies found most breathing interventions worked, and linked effectiveness to human-guided training and repeated practice rather than to fast-paced breathing alone. A 2026 randomised trial in 98 paramedicine students reported lower stress, anxiety and depression after a structured breathing programme. Most trials carried a moderate risk of bias.

catalog:recovery:stretching.evidenceSummary: A meta-analysis of 11 randomised trials with 452 people found strength training and stretching improved range of motion about equally. A larger systematic review of 65 studies with 1542 adults examined why range of motion improves, looking at stretch tolerance, passive stiffness and fascicle length. A third systematic review of randomised trials compared post-exercise stretching with other recovery methods for soreness, strength and range of motion, and rated the evidence as limited. Nothing here supports stretching on its own as injury prevention.

catalog:recovery:sunlight.evidenceSummary: A systematic review of 128 studies found that light exposure, and its timing, shifts melatonin secretion and circadian rhythm in people. A trial in 50 adults showed that morning bright light combined with afternoon melatonin advanced circadian timing over three days, with more light giving a larger shift. Two cross-sectional studies link more morning outdoor light with earlier sleep timing and better reported sleep quality. The cross-sectional parts show association only, and the trial combined light with melatonin, so light alone cannot be separated out.

In surgical patients, a meta-analysis of 16 randomised trials found compression reduced deep vein thrombosis compared with no prophylaxis, but not compared with drug prophylaxis. A meta-analysis of 14 trials in breast cancer patients found it reduced the incidence of lymphedema. Sports recovery evidence is weaker than the clinical evidence.

A safety review covering 951 female participants reported no deaths or serious adverse outcomes and no rise in gastrointestinal, kidney or liver problems.

catalog:supplement:bcaa.evidenceSummary: A meta-analysis of 18 randomised trials found branched-chain amino acids lowered creatine kinase at some time points and reduced muscle soreness over the days after damaging exercise, with no effect on lactate dehydrogenase. A systematic review of 22 trials with 511 healthy participants found soreness may fall, but effects on strength, endurance and body composition were inconsistent, and no meta-analysis was possible because of bias risk. In liver cirrhosis, a meta-analysis of five trials with 434 patients found a better frailty index, body mass index and quality of life, but no change in grip strength or muscle index.

A dataset analysis of protein quality scores found most single plant proteins score below animal proteins, while mixtures can raise the score. Evidence is small human trials plus composition data.

catalog:supplement:vitamin-a.evidenceSummary: A European Food Safety Authority opinion kept a tolerable upper intake level for preformed vitamin A, choosing birth defects as the critical harm, with liver damage and bone effects also reviewed. No upper level could be set for beta-carotene; the panel picked lung cancer risk as the critical effect of beta-carotene supplements, especially in smokers. A separate review describes laboratory evidence that excess vitamin A harms mitochondria. These are authority opinions and reviews, not trials of a supplement.

verdict.bottomLine: These sources describe vitamin A's safe upper limits and harms, including birth defects, not benefits from supplements.

catalog:supplement:vitamin-c.evidenceSummary: Small human studies show that vitamin C absorption in the gut saturates: beyond a point, taking more does not raise absorption in proportion. In an intestinal perfusion study in volunteers, absorption followed saturation kinetics, and the authors suggested very large single doses are absorbed less efficiently than smaller ones taken separately. In a four-person comparison of oral forms, about 30% of a large oral dose was recovered in urine against about 85% after injection, with a timed-release capsule lower still, and absorption varied widely between people. The NIH fact sheet is a general reference.

The sources here test absorption only, not any health outcome.
verdict.bottomLine: The evidence here covers absorption only: uptake saturates and varies between people, with no outcomes tested.

One randomised trial in 148 women with osteopenia found preserved trabecular bone structure at the tibia but no difference in bone density.

A separate six-month randomised trial in 45 middle-aged men combined the extract with training and reported better erectile function and testosterone, so the extract's own effect cannot be separated.

catalog:supplement:omega-3.evidenceSummary: A meta-analysis of 38 randomised trials with 149,051 participants found omega-3 supplements lowered cardiovascular death (RR 0.93), non-fatal heart attack, coronary heart disease events and revascularisation. Reductions were larger with EPA alone than with EPA plus DHA, but EPA alone also raised bleeding and atrial fibrillation, and omega-3 overall raised atrial fibrillation. A separate meta-analysis of 26 trials with 2,160 participants found a small overall benefit for depression symptoms, mainly with EPA-predominant formulas. Evidence is large pooled trial data.

catalog:food-protocol:omad.evidenceSummary: No linked study tested one meal a day directly. catalog:food-protocol:extended-fast.evidenceSummary: An observational study of 1,422 people in a supervised multi-day fasting programme reported falls in weight, waist circumference and blood pressure, better blood lipids and glucose control, and adverse effects in under 1% of participants. Most reported no hunger after the first days, and 84% of those with existing complaints said these improved. A narrative review of human trials adds that prolonged fasting causes moderate weight loss, of which about two-thirds is lean mass, and that metabolic gains faded a few months after refeeding. Reported problems include metabolic acidosis, headache and insomnia.

catalog:food-protocol:low-carb.evidenceSummary: A systematic review of 15 controlled trials in type 2 diabetes found that low-carbohydrate approaches, with or without calorie restriction, produced clinically meaningful weight loss and lower HbA1c, with neither approach clearly better at 12 and 24 months. Average weight loss tracked the fall in HbA1c, suggesting sustained weight loss drives remission. A meta-analysis of randomised trials (18 studies, 2,204 adults) found a modest HbA1c advantage at one year, plus better triglycerides and HDL cholesterol. Whether cutting carbohydrates helps beyond weight loss is still unclear.

catalog:food-protocol:carb-cycling.evidenceSummary: A systematic review and meta-analysis in trained endurance athletes found that periodising carbohydrate intake does not reliably improve performance compared with keeping carbohydrate high. A five-week trial in 17 well-trained cyclists found no advantage over an energy-matched high-carbohydrate diet on lactate steady state, substrate use or body composition. An eight-week trial in 24 recreational runners found fat oxidation rose on low carbohydrate and reverted when carbohydrate returned, with better running economy at lactate threshold in the periodised group but no difference in performance. Evidence is small trials plus one meta-analysis.

They also describe risks at the high end: heart tissue damage, arrhythmias and exercise-induced hypertension with very high intensity or very long distances, and rare sudden cardiac death in marathon and ultra-endurance running. The reviews conclude benefits come at moderate levels of running.

catalog:supplement:aicar.evidenceSummary: AICAR (5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide-1-β-D-ribofuranoside) is produced naturally in the body and activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). AICAR has been used clinically in select settings for myocardial protection in cardiac bypass surgery and cardiac ischemia. Importantly, many effects previously attributed to AMPK activation by AICAR are now known to be AMPK-independent.

Topical minoxidil was approved by the FDA for male pattern hair loss in 1988 and for female pattern hair loss in 1991. It is available over-the-counter in 2% and 5% solutions and 5% foam formulations in the United States. Minoxidil works by enlarging miniaturized hair follicles, extending the anagen (growth) phase of the hair cycle, and shortening the telogen (resting) phase, thereby decreasing hair loss and increasing hair thickness. It is converted to its active form, minoxidil sulfate, in the scalp by the enzyme SULT1A1. Topical minoxidil has been found safe and effective in meta-analysis with similar efficacy and safety across different concentrations.

The combination also significantly improved systolic blood pressure, waist circumference, lipid levels, and glycemic control, with 88% of prediabetic participants returning to normoglycemia. Safety profile was consistent with GLP-1 receptor agonists, primarily featuring transient mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea 55%), with low discontinuation rates (6-8.4%). catalog:medication:liraglutide.evidenceSummary: Liraglutide (Saxenda) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist approved by the FDA for chronic weight management in adults with a BMI of 30 kg/m² or higher or BMI of 27 kg/m² or greater with at least one weight-related condition, and in adolescents (ages 12-17) with obesity. FDA approval occurred on December 23, 2014, with the adolescent indication added in December 2020. Liraglutide is dosed as a once-daily injection and is used as an adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. Clinical trials showed 62% of patients on liraglutide achieved at least 5% weight loss compared to 34% on placebo. The prescribing label contains a boxed warning regarding the risk of thyroid c-cell tumors. catalog:medication:mazdutide.evidenceSummary: Mazdutide (IBI362) is a dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist developed through a partnership between Innovent Biologics and Eli Lilly. catalog:medication:orforglipron.evidenceSummary: Orforglipron (LY3502970) is an oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist being developed by Eli Lilly for obesity treatment. The ATTAIN-1 Phase III trial enrolled 3,127 adults with obesity over 72 weeks, demonstrating double-digit percentage mean weight loss, with the majority of participants achieving at least a 10% reduction and improvements in cardiometabolic parameters. The highest-efficacy regimen, taken once daily without food or water restrictions, lowered weight by a clinically meaningful margin compared with placebo, with meaningful A1C reductions and improved cardiometabolic risk factors. Orforglipron is being developed as an oral medication taken on a daily schedule. With ATTAIN-2 completion, Lilly has the clinical data package required for global regulatory submissions in 2026.

protocols.outcome: Statistically significant improvement in mental recovery scores during both the intramuscular and oral phases, with adverse events reported in a small minority of patients and good overall tolerability
protocols.duration: Twenty-eight days of intramuscular dosing followed by five months of oral dosing

source.title: A multicentre trial to evaluate the efficacy and tolerability of alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine versus cytosine diphosphocholine in patients with vascular dementia - PubMed

protocols.population: 120 patients with mild to moderate vascular dementia in an open multicentre trial
protocols.regimen: Alpha-GPC 1 g per day given intramuscularly for 90 days, compared against intramuscular cytosine diphosphocholine at the same dose
protocols.outcome: Both treatments produced symptomatic improvement on psychometric tests with good tolerability, and alpha-GPC showed statistically higher efficacy on most measures than the comparator

benefits: In clinical trials of stroke and vascular dementia patients, alpha-GPC was linked to measurable improvement in cognitive and functional test scores
Reported tolerability in these clinical populations was generally good
risks: Most supporting trials were conducted in patients with stroke or dementia rather than healthy adults, so applicability to a general population is uncertain
Mild gastrointestinal complaints, insomnia, and headache have been reported in trial participants
verdict.bottomLine: Alpha-GPC has real clinical trial support in stroke and vascular dementia populations, but evidence specific to cognitive or athletic enhancement in healthy adults is thinner and more mixed, so its benefits outside a medical context are not well established.

catalog:supplement:inositol.evidenceSummary: Inositol is a naturally occurring sugar alcohol involved in cell signaling, available in dietary and supplement forms as myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol. It has been most studied in women with polycystic ovary syndrome, where randomized trials have examined effects on insulin sensitivity, hormone levels, and ovulation. A systematic review commissioned for international PCOS treatment guidelines found some metabolic and reproductive signals but concluded the overall evidence base remains limited and inconclusive.

links.title: Inositol for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis to Inform the 2023 Update of the International Evidence-based PCOS Guidelines - PubMed
Inositol: Benefits, Dosage, and Side Effects - Examine

source.title: Inositol for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis to Inform the 2023 Update of the International Evidence-based PCOS Guidelines - PubMed

protocols.population: Thirty randomized controlled trials, 2230 women with polycystic ovary syndrome, with nineteen trials pooled in meta-analyses
protocols.regimen: Trials of myo-inositol or D-chiro-inositol, alone or combined with other therapies, compared against placebo, metformin, or each other, across the pooled evidence base
protocols.outcome: Some evidence of benefit for select metabolic measures and for D-chiro-inositol on ovulation, but the authors judged evidence for most outcomes limited and inconclusive, with myo-inositol causing fewer gastrointestinal side effects than metformin
protocols.duration: Duration varied across the thirty pooled trials

benefits: Some randomized trials suggest inositol may improve insulin-related metabolic markers in women with polycystic ovary syndrome
Appears better tolerated on the digestive system than metformin in head-to-head trials
risks: The evidence-review panel behind the 2023 international PCOS guidelines rated the overall evidence as limited and inconclusive
Most research is in women with polycystic ovary syndrome, so benefits in other populations are not established
verdict.bottomLine: Inositol shows some promising signals for metabolic and reproductive outcomes in polycystic ovary syndrome, but the guideline-informing systematic review found the evidence too limited to draw firm conclusions.

catalog:supplement:probiotic.evidenceSummary: Probiotics are live microorganisms, most often lactobacillus and bifidobacterium species, marketed in single-strain and multi-strain blends for digestive and general health. Because different genera, species, and strains behave differently, research findings for one product cannot be assumed to apply to another, and study quality varies widely across the field. Systematic reviews consistently find that effects, when present, are specific to the exact strain combination and condition studied rather than a general property of probiotics as a category.

links.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis: Multi-strain probiotics as adjunct therapy for Helicobacter pylori eradication and prevention of adverse events - PubMed
Probiotics: Benefits, Dosage, and Side Effects - Examine

source.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis: Multi-strain probiotics as adjunct therapy for Helicobacter pylori eradication and prevention of adverse events - PubMed

protocols.population: Nineteen randomized controlled trials, 2730 participants with Helicobacter pylori infection, testing twenty treatment arms across six multi-strain probiotic mixtures
protocols.regimen: Multi-strain probiotic mixtures given alongside standard antibiotic eradication therapy, compared against eradication therapy plus placebo or no adjunct, across the pooled trials
protocols.outcome: Four of the six probiotic mixtures significantly improved Helicobacter pylori eradication rates, five reduced any adverse reaction, and three reduced antibiotic-associated diarrhea, with effects specific to which strains were combined
protocols.duration: Given for the duration of standard antibiotic eradication therapy, varying by trial

benefits: Certain multi-strain combinations have improved eradication rates and reduced side effects when added to antibiotic regimens in trials
Some strain-specific formulations have trial support for irritable bowel symptom relief
risks: Benefits are strain- and condition-specific, so a positive finding for one product does not transfer to a different blend
Many published probiotic trials are small or of variable methodological quality
verdict.bottomLine: Multi-strain probiotics can help with specific, well-studied conditions when the exact strain combination matches the trial evidence, but as a broad category the evidence does not support a single generic effect across all products.

catalog:supplement:psyllium.evidenceSummary: Psyllium is a soluble, viscous fiber derived from the husk of Plantago ovata seeds, commonly used as a bulk-forming laxative and fiber supplement. Randomized controlled trials have examined its effects on chronic constipation and on blood lipid levels including LDL cholesterol. Pooled meta-analyses of these trials report consistent improvements in stool frequency for constipation and reductions in LDL and non-HDL cholesterol compared with placebo.

links.title: Effect of psyllium (Plantago ovata) fiber on LDL cholesterol and alternative lipid targets, non-HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B - PubMed
Psyllium: Benefits, Dosage, and Side Effects - Examine

source.title: Effect of psyllium (Plantago ovata) fiber on LDL cholesterol and alternative lipid targets, non-HDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B - PubMed

protocols.population: Twenty-eight randomized controlled trials, 1924 participants with or without hypercholesterolemia
protocols.regimen: Oral psyllium fiber supplementation at a median dose of about 10 grams per day for at least three weeks, compared against control diets or placebo fiber
protocols.outcome: Significant reductions in LDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, and apolipoprotein B compared with control, graded as moderate to high quality evidence by the review authors
protocols.duration: At least three weeks across the twenty-eight pooled trials

benefits: Randomized trials consistently show reductions in LDL and non-HDL cholesterol compared with control diets
Well-supported as a bulk-forming fiber for relieving chronic constipation
risks: Mild gastrointestinal effects such as bloating and gas are commonly reported, especially when starting
Product adulteration with cheaper fillers such as amaranth or wheat bran has been documented in the psyllium supplement market
verdict.bottomLine: Trial evidence solidly supports psyllium for improving cholesterol markers and relieving constipation, making it one of the better-evidenced fiber supplements on the market.

catalog:supplement:selenium.evidenceSummary: Selenium is an essential trace mineral obtained from diet, such as Brazil nuts, seafood, and organ meats, and required for antioxidant enzymes and thyroid hormone metabolism. It has an established recommended dietary allowance and has been studied both for general adequacy and in randomized trials of people with autoimmune thyroid conditions such as Hashimoto thyroiditis. Meta-analyses of these trials report reductions in thyroid-stimulating hormone and thyroid antibody levels among people without thyroid hormone replacement, alongside long-established data defining safe upper intake levels.

links.title: Selenium - Health Professional Fact Sheet - NIH Office of Dietary Supplements
Selenium Supplementation in Patients with Hashimoto Thyroiditis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials - PubMed

source.title: Selenium Supplementation in Patients with Hashimoto Thyroiditis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials - PubMed

protocols.population: Thirty-five randomized controlled trials pooled across cohorts of people with Hashimoto thyroiditis, with and without thyroid hormone replacement therapy
protocols.regimen: Oral selenium supplementation trials, commonly in the range of 80 to 200 micrograms per day for periods of three months to two years, compared against placebo
protocols.outcome: Selenium supplementation reduced thyroid-stimulating hormone and thyroid peroxidase antibody levels in patients not on hormone replacement, with comparable adverse-event rates between selenium and placebo groups and moderate overall certainty of evidence

benefits: An essential nutrient with a well-established dietary allowance target set by national nutrition authorities
Trials in people with Hashimoto thyroiditis found reductions in thyroid-stimulating hormone and thyroid antibody levels
risks: Chronic excess intake can cause selenosis, with hair and nail brittleness as characteristic signs
Benefit for thyroid antibodies has mainly been shown in people with diagnosed autoimmune thyroid disease, not the general population
verdict.bottomLine: Selenium is a well-characterized essential nutrient with a defined safe intake range, and randomized trial evidence supports a role in lowering thyroid antibody levels for people with Hashimoto thyroiditis specifically.

catalog:supplement:potassium.evidenceSummary: Potassium is an essential mineral and electrolyte required for nerve signaling, muscle contraction, and fluid balance, and it is naturally abundant in fruits, vegetables, legumes, and dairy. It is classified as an essential nutrient with a well-established adequate intake, and decades of research have examined its role in blood pressure regulation and cardiovascular health. Most healthy adults meet their needs through diet alone, and supplementation is generally reserved for documented deficiency under medical supervision.

links.title: Potassium - Health Professional Fact Sheet (NIH Office of Dietary Supplements)
Potassium - Consumer Fact Sheet (NIH Office of Dietary Supplements)

source.title: Potassium - Health Professional Fact Sheet (NIH Office of Dietary Supplements)

protocols.population: Adults with hypertension, pooled across randomized controlled trials summarized by the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements
protocols.regimen: Potassium supplements, mostly potassium chloride, at 20 to 120 mmol per day for 1 to 36 months, compared with placebo
protocols.outcome: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure decreased significantly compared with placebo, with larger effects in people with higher baseline blood pressure and lower baseline potassium intake.

benefits: Supports normal nerve and muscle function as an essential electrolyte the body cannot do without
Blood pressure reductions have been observed in supplementation trials in hypertensive populations
Adequate dietary intake is associated with lower stroke risk in large observational cohorts
risks: Impaired kidney function or medications that reduce potassium excretion, such as ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or potassium-sparing diuretics, sharply raise the danger of hyperkalemia from added potassium
Severe hyperkalemia can cause muscle weakness, paralysis, and life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias

No tolerable upper intake level has been set for potassium because the harm reported in case studies came from rapid, concentrated exposure rather than food-level intake, which argues for caution rather than reassurance with concentrated supplements
verdict.bottomLine: Potassium is essential and well studied for cardiovascular health, but it is also a rare case where supplementation carries real danger for people with kidney disease or interacting medications, making it a nutrient best supplemented only under clinical monitoring of blood levels.

catalog:supplement:5-htp.evidenceSummary: 5-HTP, or 5-hydroxytryptophan, is a naturally occurring amino acid derivative and an intermediate step in the body's conversion of tryptophan into serotonin. It has been studied mainly as a potential aid for mood and sleep, with most available trials being small, short, and methodologically limited. A Cochrane systematic review found that only a small fraction of identified studies met quality standards for inclusion, leaving the overall evidence base thin despite decades of interest.

links.title: Tryptophan and 5-hydroxytryptophan for depression - PubMed (Cochrane review)
Tryptophan and 5-Hydroxytryptophan for depression | Cochrane

source.title: Tryptophan and 5-hydroxytryptophan for depression - PubMed (Cochrane review)

protocols.population: 64 patients with depression, drawn from the only 2 trials out of 108 identified studies that met Cochrane quality criteria
protocols.regimen: 5-HTP or tryptophan preparations compared with placebo in short-term randomized trials
protocols.outcome: Both substances performed better than placebo at reducing depressive symptoms, but the reviewers concluded the evidence was insufficient in quantity and quality to support routine clinical use pending further study.
protocols.duration: Short-term, across the two trials meeting inclusion criteria

benefits: Small clinical trials suggest possible short-term improvement in depressive symptoms compared with placebo
As a direct serotonin precursor, its proposed mechanism of action is biologically plausible and well characterized
risks: Combining it with antidepressants or other serotonergic drugs raises the risk of serotonin syndrome
Most supporting trials are small, old, and short in duration, so long-term safety and effectiveness are not established
Nausea and other gastrointestinal upset are commonly reported side effects
verdict.bottomLine: Evidence for 5-HTP remains preliminary: early trials look promising but a formal Cochrane review found too few high-quality studies to support confident use, and it carries meaningful interaction risk with serotonergic medications.

catalog:supplement:nmn.evidenceSummary: NMN, or nicotinamide mononucleotide, is a naturally occurring compound and a direct precursor in the body's production of NAD+, a molecule central to cellular energy metabolism. Interest in NMN grew out of animal aging research, and it has since moved into a small but growing number of human trials examining safety and its effects on NAD+ levels, metabolism, and physical performance. Long-term human outcome data, including any effect on aging itself or chronic disease risk, remain limited.

links.title: The efficacy and safety of β-nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) supplementation in healthy middle-aged adults - PubMed

source.title: The efficacy and safety of β-nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) supplementation in healthy middle-aged adults - PubMed

protocols.population: 80 healthy middle-aged adults in a randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-dependent trial
protocols.regimen: Oral NMN once daily at 300 mg, 600 mg, or 900 mg, or a matching placebo, for 60 days
protocols.outcome: Blood NAD+ concentrations rose significantly in all treated groups in a dose-related manner, physical performance measures improved, and the compound was reported safe and well tolerated at every dose tested.

benefits: Well-designed randomized trials show NMN reliably raises blood NAD+ levels in healthy adults
Short-term trials report good tolerability with no serious adverse events
Early data point to possible benefits for physical endurance measures
risks: Long-term safety and effectiveness beyond a few months of use have not been studied in humans
Much of the foundational evidence for anti-aging effects comes from animal models and has not been confirmed in people
Regulatory status is unsettled and commercial product purity varies widely
verdict.bottomLine: NMN reliably raises NAD+ levels in short human trials and appears well tolerated, but the leap from that biomarker change to a meaningful long-term health benefit remains unproven in people.

catalog:supplement:resveratrol.evidenceSummary: Resveratrol is a polyphenol compound found in red grape skins, red wine, and certain berries, first studied for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. It has since been tested in a large number of human clinical trials across many conditions, including metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular risk factors, and polycystic ovary syndrome. A systematic review of the accumulated trials concluded that despite two decades of research, poor oral absorption and inconsistent study design have kept the evidence too weak to support any specific clinical recommendation.

links.title: Resveratrol for the Management of Human Health: How Far Have We Come? A Systematic Review of Resveratrol Clinical Trials
Resveratrol supplementation efficiently improves endothelial health: A systematic review and meta-analysis - PubMed

source.title: Resveratrol for the Management of Human Health: How Far Have We Come? A Systematic Review of Resveratrol Clinical Trials

protocols.population: Nearly 6,200 participants across 31 countries, pooled from 194 clinical trials, including 155 randomized controlled trials, published since 2004
protocols.regimen: Oral resveratrol supplementation across trials, generally well tolerated at doses up to 1 g per day, with no consensus regimen established for any single condition
protocols.outcome: Resveratrol consistently reduced inflammatory markers and improved aspects of dysregulated metabolism across studies, but the authors concluded the evidence remains insufficient for a formal clinical recommendation and called for larger, higher-quality trials.
protocols.duration: Duration varied across the 194 pooled trials

benefits: Trials consistently show reductions in inflammatory markers across many study populations
Some evidence points to improved blood vessel function and metabolic markers in specific conditions
Generally well tolerated in trials, with mostly mild gastrointestinal side effects reported
risks: Natural oral absorption is very poor, and different formulations have shown widely variable blood levels
No consensus exists on which condition, dose, or duration produces reliable benefit
Evidence quality across the field is inconsistent, dominated by small, short, early-phase trials
verdict.bottomLine: Resveratrol has one of the largest human trial bases of any dietary supplement, yet after two decades of research the evidence still falls short of supporting a specific clinical use.

catalog:supplement:tart-cherry.evidenceSummary: Tart cherry, most often studied as Montmorency tart cherry juice or concentrate, is a fruit source of anthocyanins and other polyphenols with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. It has been tested mainly in athletes and recreationally active adults for effects on muscle soreness, inflammation markers, and recovery after strenuous exercise. Trial results are mixed: some randomized studies report meaningful reductions in exercise-induced pain and strength loss, while others in different populations find no measurable benefit.

links.title: Efficacy of tart cherry juice in reducing muscle pain during running: a randomized controlled trial
No Effect of Tart Cherry Juice or Pomegranate Juice on Recovery from Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Non-Resistance Trained Men

source.title: Efficacy of tart cherry juice in reducing muscle pain during running: a randomized controlled trial

protocols.population: 54 healthy runners in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial during the Hood to Coast relay race
protocols.regimen: 355 mL of tart cherry juice or a placebo cherry drink twice daily for 7 days before the event and on race day, each bottle equivalent to roughly 45 to 50 cherries with at least 600 mg phenolic compounds and 40 mg anthocyanins
protocols.outcome: The cherry juice group reported a significantly smaller increase in post-race muscle pain (12 mm on a visual analog scale) than the placebo group (37 mm), a statistically significant difference.
protocols.duration: Seven days before the event and on race day

benefits: Several randomized trials in runners and other athletes report less muscle pain and faster strength recovery after strenuous exercise
Meta-analyses link supplementation with reductions in inflammatory markers such as IL-6 after exercise
Whole-fruit source with a well-characterized polyphenol and anthocyanin content
risks: Findings are inconsistent across studies, and some trials in non-resistance-trained populations found no measurable benefit
Many trials are small, short, and funded or supplied by cherry industry groups, which can bias reported outcomes
High sugar content in juice form is a factor for people managing blood glucose
verdict.bottomLine: Tart cherry has real randomized-trial support for easing exercise-induced soreness in some athletic populations, but the effect is inconsistent enough across studies that it cannot be called a reliable recovery aid across the board.

catalog:supplement:saw-palmetto.evidenceSummary: Saw palmetto is an extract from the berries of the Serenoa repens palm, widely marketed for lower urinary tract symptoms associated with an enlarged prostate. It is one of the most extensively studied botanical supplements, with dozens of randomized trials conducted over several decades. A Cochrane systematic review pooling this trial evidence found the extract, taken alone, provides little to no benefit over placebo for urinary symptoms or quality of life.

links.title: Serenoa repens for benign prostatic hyperplasia | Cochrane
Saw Palmetto for the Treatment of Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Due to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia - PubMed

source.title: Serenoa repens for benign prostatic hyperplasia | Cochrane

protocols.population: 4,656 men, mean age 52 to 68, with moderate lower urinary tract symptoms from benign prostatic hyperplasia, pooled across 27 randomized controlled trials
protocols.regimen: Saw palmetto extract, most commonly 320 mg per day, alone or combined with other plant extracts, compared with placebo for 3 to 17 months
protocols.outcome: Saw palmetto alone showed little to no difference from placebo in urinary symptoms or quality of life at both short-term (3 to 6 months) and long-term (12 to 17 months) follow-up, with no significant increase in adverse events.
protocols.duration: Three to seventeen months across the pooled trials

benefits: Extensively studied in dozens of randomized trials over several decades, giving unusually mature safety data for a botanical supplement
Adverse event rates in trials were similar to placebo, indicating good tolerability
risks: The largest pooled analysis available, a Cochrane systematic review, found no meaningful benefit over placebo for urinary symptoms
Relying on it in place of evaluated medical treatment for an enlarged prostate risks delaying effective care
Mild gastrointestinal upset has been reported in a minority of users
verdict.bottomLine: Saw palmetto is among the best-studied herbal supplements for prostate symptoms, and that scrutiny is exactly what undermines it: the highest-quality pooled evidence finds no real benefit over placebo.

catalog:supplement:beetroot.evidenceSummary: Beetroot, and the concentrated juice made from it, is a natural source of inorganic dietary nitrate that the body converts into nitric oxide, a molecule involved in blood vessel dilation. It has been tested in numerous randomized trials for effects on blood pressure and exercise performance, particularly in endurance and interval-based activities. Meta-analyses show a consistent, modest blood-pressure-lowering effect, while findings on exercise performance are more mixed and depend heavily on exercise type and training status.

links.title: Inorganic nitrate and beetroot juice supplementation reduces blood pressure in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis - PubMed
The Effect of Beetroot Ingestion on High-Intensity Interval Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

source.title: Inorganic nitrate and beetroot juice supplementation reduces blood pressure in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis - PubMed

protocols.population: 254 participants pooled across 16 randomized controlled trials of inorganic nitrate or beetroot juice versus placebo
protocols.regimen: Inorganic nitrate or beetroot juice supplementation, from a single acute dose up to 15 days of daily dosing, compared with a nitrate-depleted placebo
protocols.outcome: Supplementation was associated with a significant reduction in systolic blood pressure of about 4.4 mmHg, with a smaller and less consistent reduction in diastolic blood pressure.
protocols.duration: Single acute dose up to fifteen days of daily dosing

source.title: The Effect of Beetroot Ingestion on High-Intensity Interval Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

protocols.population: 319 participants, mostly recreationally active adults, pooled across 17 randomized trials of high-intensity interval or sprint training
protocols.regimen: Acute nitrate doses of about 4.8 to 12.9 mmol, or chronic daily doses of about 5.2 to 29.0 mmol for 3 to 28 days, most often given 2 to 3 hours before exercise
protocols.outcome: Beetroot supplementation produced no significant improvement in peak or mean power output during high-intensity interval or sprint training, though a small, significant improvement appeared on an intermittent running recovery test.

benefits: Randomized trials consistently show a modest reduction in blood pressure, particularly systolic pressure
Some evidence supports improved intermittent running capacity in recreationally active people
Whole-food source of nitrate with a well-understood mechanism through nitric oxide production
risks: Effects on high-intensity power output in trained or elite athletes are largely absent in pooled analyses
Urine and stool can turn red or pink after consumption, which is harmless but can be mistaken for a medical problem
Long-term cardiovascular outcome data beyond blood pressure changes are limited
verdict.bottomLine: Beetroot and dietary nitrate have some of the more consistent supplement evidence for blood pressure, but the exercise-performance story is uneven and depends heavily on the sport and the athlete's training level.

catalog:medication:insulin.evidenceSummary: Insulin glargine is a long-acting recombinant human insulin analog engineered to provide a relatively steady, once-daily basal insulin profile. It is approved by the FDA to improve glycemic control in adults and children with type 1 diabetes and in adults with type 2 diabetes, and it is not intended for treating diabetic ketoacidosis. Regulatory review covered pharmacokinetics, cardiovascular outcomes, and immunogenicity across large clinical trial programs.

protocols.duration: ongoing daily basal dosing, titrated based on periodic blood glucose monitoring
protocols.outcome: FDA-approved basal insulin analog shown in labeling trials to improve glycemic control versus comparator insulin regimens

source.title: LANTUS (insulin glargine) injection label — DailyMed

protocols.regimen: full prescribing information covering dose individualization, injection site rotation, and storage conditions for vial, cartridge, and prefilled pen presentations

Long-acting profile allows once-daily basal dosing, reviewed and labeled for use across vial, cartridge, and prefilled-pen presentations.
Decades of postmarketing surveillance data since its original approval in 2000.

Hypoglycemia, allergic reactions, and injection-site lipodystrophy are labeled adverse reactions.
Not studied in children under six years of age or in pediatric type 2 diabetes.
verdict.bottomLine: Insulin glargine is an FDA-approved long-acting basal insulin analog for type 1 and type 2 diabetes, with labeling that individualizes dosing rather than specifying a single universal amount.

catalog:medication:metformin.evidenceSummary: Metformin is a biguanide oral medication that lowers blood glucose primarily by reducing hepatic glucose production and improving peripheral insulin sensitivity. It is approved by the FDA as an adjunct to diet and exercise for improving glycemic control in adults and in pediatric patients with type 2 diabetes, and it remains the most widely prescribed first-line oral diabetes medication worldwide. Decades of clinical trial and epidemiological data cover its cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic effects.

links.title: Metformin hydrochloride tablet label — DailyMed

protocols.population: adults and pediatric patients ten years of age and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus
protocols.regimen: oral tablets starting at 500 mg twice daily or 850 mg once daily, titrated in adults to a maximum of 2550 mg per day in divided doses, and in pediatric patients to a maximum of 2000 mg per day in divided doses
protocols.duration: ongoing daily oral therapy as an adjunct to diet and exercise, with dosage adjusted based on glycemic response
protocols.outcome: FDA-approved first-line oral therapy shown in labeling trials to improve glycemic control, carrying a boxed warning for the rare risk of lactic acidosis

source.title: Metformin hydrochloride tablet label — DailyMed

benefits: First-line oral therapy for type 2 diabetes in adults and in pediatric patients ten and older.
One of the most extensively studied oral diabetes medications, with decades of clinical trial and real-world outcome data.
Labeled indication is as an adjunct to diet and exercise rather than a replacement for lifestyle management.
risks: Carries a boxed warning for lactic acidosis, a rare but serious adverse reaction more likely with renal impairment, hepatic impairment, or excessive alcohol intake.
Labeling notes potential reduction in vitamin B12 levels with long-term use.
Gastrointestinal adverse effects such as nausea and diarrhea are commonly reported.
verdict.bottomLine: Metformin is an FDA-approved, extensively studied first-line oral medication for type 2 diabetes, labeled with a boxed warning for lactic acidosis and periodic monitoring requirements.

catalog:medication:atorvastatin.evidenceSummary: Atorvastatin is a synthetic HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, or statin, that lowers LDL cholesterol by blocking an early step in hepatic cholesterol synthesis. It is approved by the FDA to reduce the risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, and other cardiovascular events in adults with elevated cardiovascular risk, and separately to lower LDL cholesterol across several inherited and acquired lipid disorders, including pediatric familial hypercholesterolemia. Its cardiovascular outcome and safety data span numerous large randomized trials.

protocols.regimen: oral tablets at a labeled starting dosage of 10 or 20 mg once daily, with a dosage range of 10 mg to 80 mg once daily individualized to therapeutic response
protocols.duration: ongoing daily therapy, with response assessed as early as four weeks after initiation or dose change
protocols.outcome: FDA-approved labeling documenting reduced risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, revascularization procedures, and angina, along with LDL cholesterol reduction across studied populations

source.title: LIPITOR (atorvastatin calcium) tablet label — DailyMed

One of the most extensively studied statins, with cardiovascular outcome trials spanning primary and secondary prevention populations.
Approved down to pediatric familial hypercholesterolemia populations under specific age and diagnostic criteria.

Not labeled for use during pregnancy or breastfeeding due to potential fetal harm.
Liver enzyme elevations are a labeled adverse reaction requiring periodic monitoring.
verdict.bottomLine: Atorvastatin is an FDA-approved, extensively studied statin for cardiovascular risk reduction and LDL lowering, labeled with monitoring requirements for muscle and liver effects.

catalog:context:sleep.evidenceSummary: Sleep duration and quality logged as their own entry let a pattern emerge across weeks that a single night's device readout cannot show. A joint consensus statement from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and the Sleep Research Society reviewed the existing evidence linking adult sleep duration to cardiovascular, metabolic, and cognitive outcomes.

links.title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult: A Joint Consensus Statement of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and Sleep Research Society
Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult (full text, PMC)

protocols.population: Adults, reviewed by a multidisciplinary consensus panel
protocols.regimen: Sleep duration compared across categories from fewer than 6 hours nightly to 9 or more hours nightly, based on a modified RAND Appropriateness Method review of existing cohort and experimental literature
protocols.duration: Consensus review of accumulated longitudinal and experimental evidence, published 2015
protocols.outcome: The panel concluded that sleeping 7 or more hours per night on a regular basis is associated with optimal health, while consistently sleeping fewer than 7 hours is associated with adverse cardiometabolic, immune, and cognitive outcomes

source.title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult: A Joint Consensus Statement of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and Sleep Research Society

benefits: Consistently sleeping seven or more hours nightly is associated with lower rates of cardiovascular disease, obesity, and impaired immune function in the consensus literature.
Logging duration over weeks reveals patterns a single night's reading cannot show.
Adequate sleep duration correlates with better next-day cognitive performance in the reviewed studies.
risks: Self-reported sleep logs can diverge from objective sleep-tracking data.
Consistently sleeping fewer than six hours nightly is linked with higher rates of hypertension, diabetes, depression, and mortality in cohort data.
Sleeping beyond nine hours nightly is also linked with adverse health outcomes in some cohorts, though the direction of cause and effect is unclear.
verdict.bottomLine: The joint AASM-SRS panel found sleeping seven or more hours nightly linked with better health outcomes in adults, based on a synthesis of existing cohort and experimental evidence rather than a new trial.

That analysis found that the consumption level associated with the lowest total health loss, combining cancer, injury, and cardiovascular outcomes, was zero drinks per week.

protocols.outcome: Risk of death and disability rose with each additional standard drink, with no threshold below which additional health protection was gained relative to abstaining

source.title: Alcohol use and burden for 195 countries and territories, 1990-2016: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2016

benefits: Logging each drink creates a record that can be compared against population-level consumption data.
Lower consumption levels are linked with lower risk across most alcohol-attributable disease categories in the Global Burden of Disease analysis.
Tracking intake over time can reveal drinking patterns not visible from memory alone.
risks: The Global Burden of Disease analysis found risk of death and disability rising with each additional drink, with zero consumption associated with the lowest total health loss.
Alcohol is linked with increased cancer risk even at levels formerly viewed as moderate.
Self-reported consumption logs are prone to underreporting in survey research.
verdict.bottomLine: Population-level analysis found no consumption level associated with net health benefit once all outcomes were combined, with risk of harm rising from the first drink onward.

catalog:context:nicotine.evidenceSummary: Logging nicotine or tobacco use as an occurrence mirrors how cohort studies quantify cigarettes smoked per day for mortality analysis. Two large prospective cohorts found that consistently smoking only a few cigarettes across adulthood still carried meaningfully higher mortality risk than never smoking.

links.title: Association of Long-term, Low-Intensity Smoking With All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality in the National Institutes of Health-AARP Diet and Health Study
Low-intensity cigarette smoking and mortality risks: a pooled analysis of prospective cohort studies in Japan

protocols.population: 290,215 adults aged 59 to 82 in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study cohort, USA
protocols.regimen: Lifetime cigarette smoking history classified into categories including fewer than 1 and 1 to 10 cigarettes per day, compared with never smokers
protocols.duration: Cohort followed from 2004-2005 baseline through the end of 2011
protocols.outcome: Consistent long-term smokers of fewer than 1 or 1 to 10 cigarettes per day had substantially higher all-cause and lung cancer mortality than never smokers

source.title: Association of Long-term, Low-Intensity Smoking With All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality in the National Institutes of Health-AARP Diet and Health Study

protocols.population: 410,294 adults across nine Japanese population-based prospective cohorts
protocols.regimen: Current smokers grouped by cigarettes per day, from 1-2 up to 6-10, compared with never smokers
protocols.duration: Cohort baseline data collected 1983 to 1994, followed prospectively for mortality
protocols.outcome: All-cause mortality risk was higher at every smoking-intensity category studied and increased further with each additional cigarette per day

source.title: Low-intensity cigarette smoking and mortality risks: a pooled analysis of prospective cohort studies in Japan

benefits: Logging each use creates an objective count that self-recall alone tends to underestimate.
A visible log of occurrences can make patterns of use easier to notice over time.
Cohort data show mortality risk drops substantially after smoking cessation, with earlier quitting linked to larger reductions in risk.
risks: Large cohort studies found even long-term smoking of ten or fewer cigarettes daily linked with meaningfully higher all-cause and lung cancer mortality than never smoking.
No level of cigarette smoking studied in these cohorts was free of added mortality risk.
Nicotine use is linked with cardiovascular and respiratory disease risk that scales with cumulative exposure.
verdict.bottomLine: Two large prospective cohorts found that even low-intensity, long-term cigarette smoking carried meaningfully higher mortality risk than never smoking, with no threshold identified as risk-free.

community.description: Smokefree.gov's quitSTART app includes tags for times or places associated with smoking urges as part of tracking a quit attempt.

catalog:context:alcohol-free-day.evidenceSummary: Logging an alcohol-free day as its own entry echoes how researchers tracked participants in the 'Dry January' abstinence challenge. Prospective cohort studies of thousands of participants linked completing a month of alcohol-free days with measurable gains in self-rated wellbeing and drinking control that persisted for months afterward.

links.title: Voluntary temporary abstinence from alcohol during "Dry January" and subsequent alcohol use
Short- and Longer-Term Benefits of Temporary Alcohol Abstinence During 'Dry January' Are Not Also Observed Among Adult Drinkers in the General Population: Prospective Cohort Study

protocols.population: 857 British adults (249 men, 608 women) participating in a month-long alcohol abstinence challenge
protocols.regimen: Baseline, one-month, and six-month follow-up questionnaires measuring alcohol consumption and drink refusal self-efficacy
protocols.duration: Six-month follow-up period after the abstinence month
protocols.outcome: Completing the alcohol-free month was linked with reduced later alcohol consumption and higher drink refusal self-efficacy at six months, without a rebound in consumption afterward

source.title: Voluntary temporary abstinence from alcohol during "Dry January" and subsequent alcohol use

protocols.population: 1,192 participants in the same alcohol abstinence challenge compared with 1,549 adult drinkers who did not attempt it
protocols.regimen: Online questionnaires in January, February, and August comparing wellbeing, drinking control, and alcohol intake between groups
protocols.outcome: Wellbeing and drinking-control gains seen among challenge completers were not observed in the comparison group of drinkers who did not attempt a month of alcohol-free days

source.title: Short- and Longer-Term Benefits of Temporary Alcohol Abstinence During 'Dry January' Are Not Also Observed Among Adult Drinkers in the General Population: Prospective Cohort Study

benefits: Completing a month of alcohol-free days was linked with higher self-rated wellbeing and greater drink-refusal self-efficacy at six-month follow-up in cohort data.
Gains in wellbeing among challenge completers held without a later rebound in consumption in the tracked cohort.
A visible log of alcohol-free days can make a pattern of moderation easier to notice over time.
risks: Benefits observed among people who completed a structured alcohol-free challenge were not observed among a comparison group of adult drinkers who did not attempt it, so logging alone may not replicate the effect.
People who sign up for alcohol-free challenges tend to be heavier drinkers than the general population, which limits how broadly these findings generalize.
Cohort designs cannot rule out that people already inclined toward healthier drinking patterns were more likely to complete the challenge.
verdict.bottomLine: Prospective cohort studies of a structured alcohol-free-month challenge found wellbeing and drinking-control gains among people who completed it, but the same gains did not appear in a comparison group of drinkers who did not attempt it.

source.title: Take the Dry January challenge - Harvard Health

catalog:food-protocol:calorie-protein-ta.evidenceSummary: Logging adherence to a daily calorie or protein target follows the same self-monitoring principle that systematic reviews link to outcomes from structured eating plans. Diaries and app-based tracking of intake were consistently associated with greater weight loss, and separately, higher total protein intake was linked with larger gains in muscle size and strength during resistance training.

links.title: Self-monitoring in weight loss: a systematic review of the literature
A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults

protocols.population: Adults enrolled in behavioral weight-management programs, drawn from 22 studies published 1993 to 2009
protocols.regimen: Self-monitoring of diet, exercise, or body weight using paper diaries, personal digital assistants, or electronic scales
protocols.duration: Review spanning sixteen years of published weight-loss intervention studies
protocols.outcome: Greater adherence to self-monitoring of dietary intake was consistently associated with greater weight loss across the reviewed studies

source.title: Self-monitoring in weight loss: a systematic review of the literature

protocols.population: 1,863 healthy adults across 49 randomised controlled trials of resistance training
protocols.regimen: Dietary protein supplementation added to resistance training programs, with total daily protein intake tracked across a wide range
protocols.duration: Resistance training programs lasting six weeks or longer across the pooled trials
protocols.outcome: Protein intake above a threshold identified in the pooled trials showed no further gains in fat-free mass, while intake below that threshold was associated with smaller strength and muscle-size gains

source.title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults

benefits: Self-monitoring of dietary intake was consistently linked with greater weight loss across the studies reviewed by Burke and colleagues.
Higher total protein intake during resistance training was linked with larger gains in strength and fat-free mass in the pooled trials.
A logged daily target gives an objective record of adherence rather than relying on memory.
risks: Protein intake beyond a threshold identified in the pooled trials showed no further gains in fat-free mass, so higher totals were not linked with proportionally greater benefit.
Most self-monitoring studies reviewed relied on self-report, a source of measurement error.
Evidence linking adherence to a target with better outcomes is largely correlational rather than causal.
verdict.bottomLine: Self-monitoring of dietary intake against a set target was consistently linked with greater weight loss, and higher protein intake during resistance training was linked with larger strength and muscle gains up to a point beyond which returns diminished.

catalog:exercise:pilates.evidenceSummary: A Cochrane systematic review pooling ten randomised controlled trials examined Pilates as an exercise-based treatment for nonspecific low back pain. Compared with minimal intervention, Pilates was linked with reduced pain and disability in the short and medium term, though evidence did not show it outperforming other exercise programs.

links.title: Pilates for low back pain
Pilates for Low Back Pain: Complete Republication of a Cochrane Review

protocols.population: 510 participants with acute, subacute, or chronic nonspecific low back pain across ten randomised controlled trials
protocols.regimen: Pilates-based exercise programs compared against minimal intervention or against other forms of exercise therapy
protocols.duration: Short-term and intermediate-term follow-up periods across the pooled trials, review published 2015
protocols.outcome: Pilates reduced pain and disability more than minimal intervention with low-to-moderate quality evidence, but showed no clear advantage over other exercise types

source.title: Pilates for low back pain

benefits: Pilates was linked with reduced pain and disability compared with minimal intervention in the pooled trials, with low-to-moderate quality evidence.
Effects on pain persisted at intermediate-term follow-up in several of the pooled trials.
The pooled trials found effect sizes ranging from small to medium compared with minimal intervention.
risks: The reviewers found no conclusive evidence that Pilates outperformed other forms of exercise therapy for low back pain.
Trial quality varied, with three of the ten pooled trials rated at high risk of bias.
Sample sizes in the pooled trials were modest, totaling 510 participants across ten trials.
verdict.bottomLine: A Cochrane systematic review found Pilates linked with reduced pain and disability for low back pain compared with minimal intervention, but found no clear advantage over other exercise types.

catalog:exercise:climbing.evidenceSummary: A waitlist-controlled pilot trial tested an eight-week bouldering group program as a treatment for depression, integrating psychotherapeutic elements into indoor rock-climbing sessions without ropes. Participants who bouldered showed a significantly greater drop in depression scores than the waitlist group, an early signal that structured climbing sessions may support mood.

links.title: Indoor rock climbing (bouldering) as a new treatment for depression: study design of a waitlist-controlled randomized group pilot study and the first results

protocols.population: 47 adults with depression completing a waitlist-controlled pilot study in Germany
protocols.regimen: Eight weekly three-hour bouldering group sessions combining structured indoor rock-climbing with brief psychotherapeutic interventions
protocols.duration: Eight-week intervention period with measurement at baseline and eight-week follow-up
protocols.outcome: The bouldering group showed a significantly larger reduction in Beck Depression Inventory scores than the waitlist group, with a number needed to treat of four

source.title: Indoor rock climbing (bouldering) as a new treatment for depression: study design of a waitlist-controlled randomized group pilot study and the first results

benefits: The bouldering group showed a significantly larger drop in depression scores than the waitlist group in this pilot trial.
The number needed to treat was four, meaning a meaningful benefit was attributable to the program for roughly one in four participants.
The eight-week structure combined physical activity with group-based psychotherapeutic elements.
risks: This was a pilot study with a modest sample of 47 participants, and the authors called for further research before drawing firm conclusions.
The comparison group was a waitlist rather than an active control, which can inflate apparent effect sizes.
Findings on bouldering as a depression treatment have not yet been replicated at scale.
verdict.bottomLine: An early waitlist-controlled pilot trial found an eight-week bouldering group program linked with a significantly greater reduction in depression scores than no treatment, though replication in larger trials is still needed.

catalog:exercise:team-sport.evidenceSummary: A cross-sectional analysis of self-reported data from over 1.2 million adults in the United States compared self-reported mental health burden across different exercise categories. Popular team sports were linked with the largest reduction in poor mental health days relative to not exercising, ahead of cycling and gym-based activity.

links.title: Association between physical exercise and mental health in 1·2 million individuals in the USA between 2011 and 2015: a cross-sectional study

protocols.population: 1,237,194 adults aged 18 and older from the 2011, 2013, and 2015 CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System survey, USA
protocols.regimen: Self-reported exercise type, frequency, duration, and intensity compared against self-reported days of poor mental health in the past month, matched for demographic and health covariates
protocols.duration: Cross-sectional survey data collected across three survey years, 2011 to 2015
protocols.outcome: Individuals who exercised reported fewer poor mental health days than matched non-exercisers, with the largest association seen for popular team sports, followed by cycling and gym-based aerobic activity

source.title: Association between physical exercise and mental health in 1·2 million individuals in the USA between 2011 and 2015: a cross-sectional study

benefits: Individuals who exercised reported fewer poor mental health days than matched non-exercisers, with popular team sports showing the largest association among exercise types studied.
The team-sport association held after matching for age, income, education, and prior depression diagnosis.
Durations around forty-five minutes and frequencies of three to five times weekly were linked with the greatest reductions in poor mental health days.
risks: This was a cross-sectional, self-reported dataset, so the analysis cannot establish that team sport participation causes better mental health rather than reflecting it.
People with more severe mental health burden may be less able to participate in team sports in the first place, a pattern the study design cannot rule out.
The largest reported association does not mean more exercise was uniformly better; very high exercise volumes did not show additional benefit in the dataset.
verdict.bottomLine: A large cross-sectional analysis of self-reported data found popular team sports linked with the largest reduction in poor mental health days among exercise types studied, though the design cannot establish cause and effect.

catalog:recovery:acupuncture.evidenceSummary: An individual patient data meta-analysis pooled results from 39 randomised trials and over 20,000 patients to compare acupuncture against sham or no-acupuncture control for chronic musculoskeletal pain, osteoarthritis, headache, and shoulder pain. Acupuncture outperformed both comparators, with treatment effects persisting a year later.

links.title: Acupuncture for Chronic Pain: Update of an Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis

protocols.population: 20,827 patients with chronic musculoskeletal pain, osteoarthritis, chronic headache, or shoulder pain, pooled across 39 randomised trials
protocols.regimen: Acupuncture needling compared against sham acupuncture or against no-acupuncture control across the pooled trials
protocols.duration: Trials published through December 2015, with outcomes measured up to one year after treatment
protocols.outcome: Acupuncture reduced pain and improved function relative to both sham and no-acupuncture control across all four pain conditions, with only a small decline in effect size at one year

source.title: Acupuncture for Chronic Pain: Update of an Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis

benefits: Acupuncture outperformed both sham and no-acupuncture control for musculoskeletal pain, osteoarthritis, headache, and shoulder pain across the pooled patient data.
Treatment effects persisted with only a small decline at one year in the pooled analysis.
The meta-analysis drew on individual patient data from 39 trials, a stronger design than pooling only summary statistics.
risks: Effect sizes versus sham control were smaller than effect sizes versus no-treatment control, indicating part of the benefit may reflect nonspecific or placebo-related mechanisms.
Effect sizes varied by trial and were sensitive to the intensity of the control-arm intervention.
The review covered a limited set of pain conditions and cannot be generalized to other complaints.
verdict.bottomLine: An individual patient data meta-analysis of 39 trials found acupuncture more effective than sham or no-acupuncture control for several chronic pain conditions, with effects persisting a year after treatment.

catalog:recovery:hyperbaric-oxygen.evidenceSummary: A prospective crossover clinical trial tested hyperbaric oxygen therapy in sixty women diagnosed with fibromyalgia syndrome, pairing symptom and quality-of-life measures with brain imaging. The treated group showed improvement across fibromyalgia symptoms alongside measurable changes in brain activity patterns linked to pain processing.

links.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy can diminish fibromyalgia syndrome--prospective clinical trial

protocols.population: 60 female patients aged 21 to 67 diagnosed with fibromyalgia syndrome for at least two years
protocols.regimen: Forty hyperbaric oxygen sessions delivered five days a week, ninety minutes each, breathing pure oxygen at two atmospheres absolute, compared against a no-treatment control period
protocols.duration: Forty-session protocol delivered over eight weeks, with crossover-control comparison
protocols.outcome: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy was linked with significant improvement in fibromyalgia symptoms and quality of life, alongside rectification of abnormal brain activity patterns on imaging, while the no-treatment control period showed no improvement

source.title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy can diminish fibromyalgia syndrome--prospective clinical trial

benefits: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy was linked with significant improvement in fibromyalgia symptoms and quality-of-life measures in this crossover trial.
Brain imaging in the treated group showed rectification of abnormal activity patterns linked to pain processing.
The crossover design let each participant serve as their own control, strengthening the comparison.
risks: The no-treatment control period showed no improvement, underscoring that benefits were specific to the oxygen therapy sessions rather than to time or attention alone.
The trial enrolled only sixty female patients from a single center, limiting how broadly the findings generalize.
Hyperbaric chambers carry known risks including barotrauma and oxygen toxicity that are not addressed by this trial's design.
verdict.bottomLine: A prospective crossover trial found a forty-session hyperbaric oxygen protocol linked with improved fibromyalgia symptoms and altered brain activity patterns, based on a small single-center sample.

catalog:recovery:gratitude-therapy.evidenceSummary: Three linked experiments randomly assigned adults to keep weekly or daily records focused on gratitude, hassles, or neutral life events. Participants in the gratitude condition consistently reported more positive affect and fewer physical symptoms than comparison groups, with a parallel benefit observed among people living with neuromuscular disease.

links.title: Counting blessings versus burdens: an experimental investigation of gratitude and subjective well-being in daily life

protocols.population: Undergraduate and community adults across two studies, plus a group of adults living with neuromuscular disease in a third study
protocols.regimen: Weekly or daily written records focused on gratitude compared against records of hassles or neutral life events
protocols.duration: Study periods ranging from two to ten weeks, published 2003
protocols.outcome: The gratitude-focused groups showed higher positive affect and better self-reported physical health than comparison groups across the three studies

source.title: Counting blessings versus burdens: an experimental investigation of gratitude and subjective well-being in daily life

benefits: Participants in the gratitude condition reported more positive affect than comparison groups across three linked studies.
A parallel benefit appeared among people living with neuromuscular disease, extending the finding beyond a general population.
Effects appeared with sessions as brief as a weekly written record.
risks: Effects were not uniform across every outcome measured; some measures showed no significant difference between conditions.
The original studies relied on self-report measures of affect and physical symptoms.
Study durations were short, ranging from two to ten weeks, so long-term persistence of the effect is not established.
verdict.bottomLine: Randomized comparisons found a gratitude-focused writing practice linked with higher positive affect than comparison conditions across three linked studies, most robustly on measures of positive affect.
